sources.label: Iute, Insurance Product Lead role description
Iute careers, customer promise and values

facts.text: Insurance intermediation represented 5% of Group revenue in 2025; Iute also reported fully digital MTPL in Albania and preparation of a subscription proposition combining travel, life and roadside assistance.
In 6M 2026, insurance brokerage revenue grew 59.6% year on year to 5.7% of total revenue; standalone motor and health products were targeted for later in 2026.
Iute Affinity publicly describes full-lifecycle administration, claims handling, partner coordination and multi-market standardisation as part of its role.

opportunities.name: Standalone motor
opportunities.note: Illustrative worked example — not a roadmap recommendation

Customer: Avoid legal, financial and mobility disruption
Current alternative and renewal behaviour to validate
Product: Core cover with an optional assistance layer
Limits, exclusions and proof of insurance must be legible
Trust bridge between digital policy and physical expectations
Business: Premium, commission and renewal are internal inputs
Model contribution after service, payment and exception costs
Test incremental adoption, not exposed-customer conversion alone
Partner: Carrier owns underwriting according to contract
Agree quote, bind, claims, data and escalation obligations
Assess portfolio sustainability, not only launch price
Operations: Policy changes, cancellation and refunds need named owners
Payment and issuance states must reconcile
A claim cannot expose the customer to partner complexity
Scale: Reuse orchestration, objects and event taxonomy
Localise carrier, wording, pricing, disclosures and claims
Extract shared capability only after pilot evidence

opportunities.name: Health + assistance
opportunities.note: Illustrative comparison — requires deeper customer and privacy evidence

Customer: Households seeking access and cost certainty
Need intensity may be high but benefit comprehension varies
Interview buyers, abandoners, users and cancellers
Product: Protection and service bundle must be evaluated separately
Waiting periods, networks and exclusions shape value
Validate whether annual or subscription framing is clearer
Business: Renewal value requires sustained perceived usefulness
Acquisition outside existing relationships may change the case
Partner: Carrier, assistance and medical networks may differ
Data boundaries and service SLAs are product constraints
Operations: Sensitive data requires purpose and access discipline
Service routing should feel like one front door
Scale: Coverage and provider networks vary materially
Shared policy wallet and service intake may still repeat
Local privacy and health regulation require validation

opportunities.name: Travel protection
opportunities.note: Illustrative comparison — test event observability and frequency

Customer: Traveller facing episodic financial and service risk
Purchase moment can be observable or explicitly declared
Validate frequency, trust and willingness to pay
Product: Territory, trip duration and exclusions must be clear
Service access may matter more than feature count
Business: Episodic purchase and annual cover have different economics
Model paid acquisition only if existing reach is insufficient
Renewal and cross-product value need evidence
Partner: Real-time policy and emergency-service availability matter
Assess claims data and incident escalation
Operations: Offline access to policy and help
Carrier outage cannot block emergency intake
Scale: Common journey with market-specific eligibility and wording
Use shared events and reconciliation controls

wireframes.title: Contextual entry
wireframes.screenCopy: Your current cover may be due for renewal soon.
wireframes.customerJob: Is this relevant to me, and why now?
wireframes.decision: Use a contextual entry only when a legitimate signal exists; otherwise use explicit discovery.
wireframes.data: Declared vehicle context or an approved lifecycle signal. Never manufacture relevance.
wireframes.metric: Incremental qualified product-detail engagement, with core-flow and opt-out guardrails.
wireframes.control: Show the reason for the offer and provide an easy way to dismiss it.

wireframes.title: Eligibility + profile
wireframes.screenCopy: We know your name and date of birth. Please confirm what can be reused.
wireframes.customerJob: Get a quote without answering the same questions twice.
wireframes.decision: Prefill only verified, permitted fields and ask for confirmation where accuracy matters.
wireframes.data: Known by Iute ≠ permitted for this purpose ≠ required by the carrier.
wireframes.control: A clear not-eligible path explains the result and any genuine alternative.

wireframes.title: Quote + choice
wireframes.screenCopy:
Essential
Required third-party cover

Plus
Cover + roadside assistance
wireframes.decision: Two useful choices are preferable to a catalogue of marginal variants.
wireframes.data: Quote ID, expiry, product version, limits, excess and carrier response.
wireframes.metric: Quote returned → informed selection; not card clicks.
wireframes.control: Never hide important limits or reframe contractual meaning.

wireframes.title: Coverage comprehension
wireframes.screenCopy:
Covered
Third-party liability

Important limit
Roadside assistance has usage limits

Not covered
Events outside the policy terms
wireframes.screenMeta: Approved wording remains the source of truth
wireframes.customerJob: Know what I am buying before I pay.
wireframes.decision: Put useful cover, material limits and exclusions in the decision path.
wireframes.data: Approved, versioned product documents and local disclosure rules.
wireframes.metric: Comprehension signal, bind rate and post-sale coverage contacts.
wireframes.control: GenAI may simplify approved content but cannot create contractual meaning.

wireframes.title: Confirm + bind
wireframes.screenCopy:
Product • price • billing • start date

Review required information and confirm payment.
wireframes.customerJob: Know whether I am insured after I pay.
wireframes.decision: Treat payment and policy issuance as separate, observable states.
wireframes.data: Consent record, idempotency key, payment status, bind status, policy ID.
wireframes.metric: Payment-to-policy issuance success and time to confirmed cover.
wireframes.control: If payment succeeds but bind fails, show pending—not active—then retry safely or refund.

wireframes.title: Policy home
wireframes.screenCopy:
Motor protection

Cover • documents • payment
Renewal date • change or cancel
wireframes.customerJob: Use and verify my cover after purchase.
wireframes.decision: Optimise for ownership, service and renewal—not only checkout.
wireframes.data: Policy version, documents, payment, changes, renewal and claim status.
wireframes.metric: Self-service completion, contact rate, renewal and claim initiation success.
wireframes.control: Provide printable proof when physical documentation still supports trust.

wireframes.title: Claim + service
wireframes.screenCopy:
Submitted ✓
Evidence checked ✓
Review in progress
Decision pending
wireframes.screenMeta: Next update: a committed service date
wireframes.customerJob: Know what is happening and what I need to do next.
wireframes.decision: A single front door should hide routing complexity without hiding accountability.
wireframes.data: Policy, claim, evidence, routing owner, SLA and status history.
wireframes.metric: Evidence-complete time, contacts per claim, TAT, reopen and complaints.
wireframes.control: Models can structure intake; coverage and claim decisions remain appropriately controlled.

questions.question: Where is the largest constraint today: product breadth, penetration, renewal, standalone distribution or operating scale?
Which constraint most often stops a promising proposition from scaling: customer price, Iute contribution, service cost or carrier economics?
Which differences between countries have proved structurally important, rather than merely local implementation detail?
Where does Iute want stronger ownership across proposition, administration, servicing and claims—and where is carrier ownership the better choice?
Where do customer and operational failures concentrate today: quote, issue, payment, servicing, claims, reconciliation or data handoffs?
What have the strongest product leads at Iute learned about moving quickly across Group, country, technology and insurance teams?
